newsitem.title: CHINA: China foreign investment to rise yearly 10.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: China foreign investment to rise yearly 10.2 pct.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in China is expected to rise an average 10.2 percent a year from 1996 to 2000, to total $230-270 billion in the five-year period, the Overseas Edition of the People's Daily said on Monday.

The preliminary estimate by the State Statistical Bureau had been worked out on the basis of China's economic targets for 1996-2000 of 8.0 percent annual economic growth and a stable exchange rate of 8.35 yuan to the dollar, the newspaper said.

State statisticians had calculated that if annual economic growth was around 8.0 percent, China would need $50 billion in direct foreign investment each year. If annual growth rose to 9.0 percent, $90 billion would be required.
Foreign investment should be controlled to ensure it accorded with China's long-term economic plans and an appropriate rate of economic growth, it said.
